[MUQATIL:16:94-97/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Wealth people possess perishes, while the reward with God in the Hereafter is lasting; those who persevere in fulfilling covenants receive the best reward and have sins overlooked.
[MUQATIL:16:94-97/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The verse was revealed about Imru al-Qays ibn Abbas al-Kindi when Abdan ibn Ashra al-Hadrami judged his claim to land and a house.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r3] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · يحيى | reports | Yahya relates that two men from a delegation of Kindah and Hadramawt disputed over land; the Hadrami accused Imruʾ al-Qays of taking part of his property, but had no formal proof.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r4] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet asked for proof, then ordered Imruʾ al-Qays to swear; the claimant warned that he was wicked and would swear falsely.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r5] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet warned that whoever takes a Muslim’s property with a false oath will meet God while God is angry with him.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r6] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · يحيى | reports | When Imruʾ al-Qays rose to swear, the verses were revealed; al-Ashʿath told him that one verse concerned him and the other his companion.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r7] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · امرؤ القيس | reports | After the verses were recited to him, Imruʾ al-Qays accepted that his own property would perish while his companion would be rewarded for his deeds.
[TAB-FULL:v14p349/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | All worldly possessions, however plentiful, perish, while the good things God has for those who fulfill His covenant and obey Him endure; one should work for and desire what lasts.
[TAB-FULL:v14p349/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God rewards those patient in obedience through ease and hardship with the best of their deeds, overlooking worse deeds, and graciously forgives their bad ones.
[TAB-FULL:v14p349/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God will also forgive their bad deeds by His grace.
[NAHHAS:v2p407/r12] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | ما عندكم is a subject and ينفد its predicate.
[NAHHAS:v2p407/r13] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | وما عند الله باق is another subject-predicate construction.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r1] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · ابن كثير وعاصم | reports | Ibn Kathir and Asim read the promise with first-person plural nūn: wa-lanajziyanna.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r2] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي | reports | Nafi, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai read the verb with third-person yāʾ: wa-layajziyanna.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r3] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · علي بن نصر عن أبي عمرو | reports | Ali ibn Nasr transmits a nūn reading from Abu Amr, agreeing with Asim.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p78/r1] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · author | holds | The yāʾ fits the preceding statement that what is with God remains; nūn has the same meaning as yāʾ. The following ولنجزينهم is unanimously read with nūn. | mentions 16:97
[SULAMI:v1p373#3/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | Obedient acts that come from people are transient, while God's recompense for those acts endures forever; the transient cannot equal what lasts.
[SULAMI:v1p373#3/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | Another says human obedience is flawed, whereas God's reward and recompense for it remain forever.
[SULAMI:v1p373#3/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · ابن عطاء | reports | Ibn Ata says human attributes perish while spiritual states endure; the servant must relinquish self-attributes and abide with God, since what comes from God remains.
[SULAMI:v1p373#3/r4] SULAMI, d. 412 · جعفر | reports | Ja'far identifies what people have as obligatory and supererogatory deeds, and what is with God as His attributes and qualities: originated things perish, while the pre-eternal remains.
[SULAMI:v1p373#3/r5] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو عثمان | reports | Abu Uthman says patience is rewarded by God's granting the servant contentment; one who truly follows the path of the patient receives the best reward in this life and the next.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | What people possess refers to the transient world, while what is with God is the enduring afterlife.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Alternatively, acts of obedience end, but their reward remains.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r1] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · ويقال | reports | What people possess of their gnoses and beloved things consists of successive traces and alternating kinds: their entities pass away, although their effects remain.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r2] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · ويقال | reports | God’s mercy, love, and constancy toward people are eternal attributes and everlasting qualities.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r3] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · ويقال | reports | Another reading says people’s longing to meet God may vanish, while His own welcome and favor toward them never end.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r4] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | A verse of poetry says that the righteous long greatly to meet God, while God longs even more to meet them.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r5] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The reward of patience is attaining one’s desired object, though the outcomes of different kinds of patience vary.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r6] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Those who patiently endure hardship in God’s cause receive immense recompense, as promised in 39:10. | mentions 39:10
[QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r7] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Those who restrain desire and avoid a lapse for God’s sake receive the chamber as their reward, as stated in 25:75. | mentions 25:75
[QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r8] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Those who remain patient under God’s decree, certain they are under His regard, are met by God’s companionship, as in 2:153. | mentions 2:153
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | What people possess runs out and means the transient world; what is with God is lasting reward and honor.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the reward never runs out: whatever is taken or eaten is replaced; this refutes those who say Paradise's pleasures will end.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the patient are those steadfast in their religion and in avoiding what God forbade.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The best deeds mean acts of obedience: permissible good actions deserve no reward, while obedience is the best and earns the promised reward; rewarding by the best deeds entails forgiveness of sins.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The passage warns against false oaths and urges people to fulfill covenants and oaths.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi says these verses were revealed about Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿAbis al-Kindi and his opponent ʿAydan ibn Ashwaʿ over a parcel of land; as Imruʾ al-Qays prepared to swear, he wept and admitted the other's right.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | What people possess in this world perishes, while God's reward and honor remain.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Those patient in faith and avoiding prohibitions are rewarded according to the best of their deeds, their acts of obedience.
[DAMGHANI:v1p16/r6] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Ajr can mean the reward for obedience; the source also glosses the Prophet's reward as thawāb. | mentions 10:72
[DAMGHANI:v1p332/r18] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | ʿInda Allāh can refer to God's reward, which remains.
[DAMGHANI:v1p75/r7] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Bāqī can mean lasting or enduring, as in what remains with God and what is better and more lasting. | mentions 28:60
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي وأبو هاشم | reports | Abū ʿAlī and Abū Hāshim say persistence needs no additional attribute; it is simply continued existence.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r11] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أكثر المفسرين | reports | Most exegetes say that substance persists.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r12] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو هاشم | reports | Abū Hāshim says not all substance persists.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r13] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الحشوية | reports | The Ḥashwiyya say all substance persists.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r14] JISHUMI, d. 494 · مشايخنا | reports | The author's teachers say that some substance persists and some does not, with further disagreement over the details.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · ابن كثير ويعقوب | reports | Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb retain the yāʾ when stopping on باق; the other readers drop it at pause, while all read tanwīn in connected speech.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Retaining the yāʾ follows the original form; dropping it at pause is for ease, and connected recitation uses tanwīn without disagreement.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو جعفر وابن كثير وعاصم | reports | These readers use first-person plural, a majestic self-reference by God.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الباقون | reports | The others use third-person ya, whose pronoun refers back to God in وما عند الله باق.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | نفاد means running out or perishing; the verb أفند describes a group's provisions running out.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The root is also used of disputants who exhaust an opponent's proof and of reciprocal disputation; a cited hadith uses نافدتهم.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Bāqī is that whose existence continues, either without interruption or simply as persistent existence; its opposite is what has perished.
[JISHUMI:v6p4105/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو القاسم | reports | Abū al-Qāsim says a thing persists through a distinct attribute of persistence.

 holds | What people possess is the perishing world; what is with God endures.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r10] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن كثير وعاصم | reports | Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read ‘We will reward’ with nūn.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r11] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الباقون | reports | The remaining readers use yāʾ for ‘He will reward.’
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r13] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Their patience is restraint from desires and endurance of obedience’s hardships, especially resisting the desire to earn money by the prohibited methods just described.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r14] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | ‘According to the best’ means in proportion to the best of what they used to do.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Worldly goods expire or their owners pass away from them, whereas the gifts of the afterlife endure forever.
[TABRISI:16:95-100/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | After the Messenger recited the covenant verses, Imruʾ al-Qays admitted taking another man's land and offered the land owed plus compensation for its fruit; 16:97 was then revealed about him.
[TABRISI:16:96-100/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | God's reward is better because what is with God remains while worldly enjoyment passes away.
[TABRISI:16:96-100/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Those who persist patiently in obedience and in keeping covenants will receive their reward.
[TABRISI:16:96-100/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The best deeds here are obedience, both obligations and recommended acts; merely permissible acts earn neither reward nor praise.
[TABRISI:16:96-100/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | rejects | The wording shows that some good can be better than other good, contrary to the claim that no good is better than good.
[TABRISI:16:96/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو جعفر وابن كثير وعاصم وعياش عن أبي عمرو | reports | Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathīr, and ʿĀṣim read with first-person plural nūn; ʿAyyāsh reports this from ʿAmr too.
[TABRISI:16:96/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Mā ʿindakum is subject with yanfadu as predicate, and mā ʿinda Allāh with bāqin; the plural pronoun follows man by sense.
[TABRISI:16:96/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · الباقون | reports | Other readers use yāʾ, supported by what is with God enduring; nūn has the same meaning.
[TABRISI:16:96/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Nafād means perishing; nafida means something ran out, and anfada describes provisions running out.
[TABRISI:16:96/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Nāfadtu means contending by trying to exhaust an opponent's proof; one report says debaters will outdo you, another transmission has qāftu.
[TABRISI:16:96/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Bāqī can mean continuously existent or existent without interruption; its opposite ceases to exist after having existed.
[TABRISI:16:96/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · البلخي | reports | Al-Balkhī says an enduring thing remains by a quality called baqāʾ.
[TABRISI:16:96/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · الأكثرون | reports | Most theologians say no separate attribute is needed; baqāʾ is continuation of existence.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Ajr is compensation received under a contract for the use of benefits; to hire someone is to assign a wage for an act.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Ajr also means setting a bone; ijār is a roof without a surrounding barrier, with plural forms ajājīr and ajājirah, and injār is a variant.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r6] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أهل التفسير | reports | The fourth sense is reward for obedience, promised to those who are patient according to their best deeds.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أهل التفسير | reports | Baqiyyah can mean permanence: what is with God endures, and what is with people passes away.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أبو زكريا | reports | Mā may be a relative noun meaning ‘that which,’ as in what people possess passing away and what God possesses enduring.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أبو زكريا | reports | As a noun, mā can also be interrogative, conditional, or an indefinite noun qualified by what follows.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r7] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · ابن قتيبة | reports | Ibn Qutayba says mā and man share an origin: man is used for people, while mā is used for other things.

[RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Faith binds a believer both to remain steadfast in Islam without reverting and to perform all the obligations and requirements of its law.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | God encourages steadfastness in Islam by rewarding the patient according to their best deeds; people earn reward for recommended and obligatory acts, not merely permitted acts.

[RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | If a worldly blessing is noble, knowing it will end spoils its enjoyment and its loss intensifies grief; if it is base, an enduring good is plainly better.

[QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | A second anonymous poem says even a freely gained world must pass away, like shade that briefly shelters before disappearing.
[QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Those who persevere are patient in Islam and obedience and refrain from sins.
[QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The best deeds are acts of obedience; they are called best because other good actions are merely permissible, and promised reward is for obedience.

[NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Those who endured the unbelievers' persecution and Islam's hardships receive their reward according to the best of their deeds.
